info.title: CineXplorer API
info.description: A modern, type-safe API for the CineXplorer movie discovery application. Authentication uses Bearer access tokens in the Authorization header, with refresh tokens stored only in HTTP-only cookies, and falls back to Django sessions for Google and GitHub sign-in.

post.description:
Register a new user and send email verification.

Creates a new user account and triggers email verification via
django-allauth CustomAccountAdapter.

Args:
    request: HTTP request object
    payload: Registration data (username, email, password, first_name, last_name)

Returns:
    Status: the status code and response data
        - 201: User created successfully, verification email sent
        - 400: Password validation failed (too weak, common, or similar to user attributes)
        - 409: Username/email already exists or forbidden username
        - 500: Email sending failed (user creation rolled back)

Password validation:
    - Enforced at schema level: min_length=8 (Pydantic)
    - Enforced at registration: Django password validators
      (common passwords, user similarity, etc.)

Email verification flow:
    1. User created with Django's create_user()
    2. EmailAddress.objects.add_email() creates EmailAddress record and sends confirmation
    3. User receives email with verification link via CustomAccountAdapter (ZeptoMail)
    4. Email verification handled by allauth EmailAddress model

Obtain JWT access and refresh tokens (login) for hybrid authentication.

Hybrid Authentication Architecture:
- Authenticates user with username/email and password
- Returns access token in response body (frontend stores in localStorage)
- Sets refresh token as HTTP-only cookie (XSS-proof, secure)
- Access token has 5-minute lifetime (short-lived, reduces XSS risk)
- Refresh token has 14-day lifetime (long-lived, stored securely)

Args:
    request: HTTP request object
    response: HTTP response object (for setting refresh token cookie)
    payload: Login credentials (login, password)

Returns:
    Status: the status code and response data
        - 200: Authentication successful, access token in body, refresh token in cookie
        - 400: Missing credentials
        - 401: Invalid credentials
        - 403: Email not verified

Response body includes:
    - access_token: JWT access token for browser storage (frontend manages)
    - user_id: Authenticated user's ID
    - email_verified: Email verification status

Cookie attributes (refresh token only):
    - httponly: True (prevents JavaScript access)
    - secure: True (HTTPS only)
    - samesite: Lax (CSRF protection)

Refresh JWT access token for hybrid authentication.

Hybrid Authentication Architecture:
- Reads refresh token from HTTP-only cookie (secure, XSS-proof)
- Returns new access token in response body (frontend stores in localStorage)
- Does NOT set access token as cookie (frontend manages it)
- Rotates refresh token in HTTP-only cookie (automatic blacklisting)

This endpoint supports the hybrid auth pattern where:
- Short-lived access tokens (5 min) in localStorage for instant auth checks
- Long-lived refresh tokens (14 days) in HTTP-only cookies for security

Args:
    request: HTTP request object
    response: HTTP response object (for setting new refresh token cookie)

Returns:
    Status: the status code and response data
        - 200: New access token in response body, refresh token rotated in cookie
        - 400: No refresh token found or invalid token format
        - 401: Token blacklisted (reuse attempt detected)

Security:
    - Token rotation: New refresh token issued on each refresh
    - Automatic blacklisting: Old tokens blacklisted via BLACKLIST_AFTER_ROTATION
    - Reuse detection: Blacklisted token attempts logged as security events

Revoke the refresh token and clear its cookie (hybrid authentication).

No authentication is required, so sign-out remains available when credentials
are missing, expired or already revoked. CSRF protection still applies.
A valid refresh token is blacklisted before its cookie is cleared; unexpected
persistence failures use the API's standard server-error response.

The frontend clears its stored access token separately. Cookie deletion uses
matching path, domain and SameSite attributes for reliable browser removal.

Args:
    request: HTTP request object containing the optional refresh cookie
    response: HTTP response object for deleting the refresh cookie

Returns:
    Status: 200 and a confirmation message after sign-out succeeds

get.description:
Get CSRF token for AJAX requests.

Generates a CSRF token using Django's built-in get_token() and ensures
it's available as a cookie that JavaScript can read. This endpoint requires
no authentication and is used by the frontend to obtain a CSRF token for
state-changing requests.

Args:
    request: HTTP request object
    response: HTTP response object (for setting cookie)

Returns:
    Status: the status code and response data
        - 200: CSRF token generated and set as cookie

Cookie details:
    - Name: 'csrftoken' (Django's default, configurable via CSRF_COOKIE_NAME)
    - httponly: False (must be readable by JavaScript per CSRF_COOKIE_HTTPONLY setting)
    - secure: True in production (per CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE setting)
    - samesite: Lax (per SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE setting)
    - path: / (available everywhere)

Note:
    Django's CsrfViewMiddleware will automatically set the csrftoken cookie
    when get_token() is called. The token is returned in the response body
    for client convenience. We force the cookie to be set even if middleware
    doesn't set it automatically.

Retrieve authenticated user's profile.

Returns the current user's profile information including computed fields
for email verification status and full name.

Args:
    request: HTTP request object with authenticated user

Returns:
    UserProfileSchema: User profile with computed fields

Raises:
    HttpError: 401 if user is not authenticated

Computed fields:
    - email_verified: Checked via allauth EmailAddress model
    - full_name: Concatenated first_name + last_name

post.description:
Verify user's email address using the confirmation key.

Supports both HMAC-based confirmations (default) and database-stored confirmations.

Args:
    request: Django HTTP request
    payload: Email verification input with confirmation key

Returns:
    Success message if verification succeeds, error if key is invalid/expired

Resend email verification using an opaque token from sign-in.

Args:
    request: Django HTTP request
    payload: Resend token issued after sign-in requires email verification

Returns:
    Generic 200 confirmation, a 400 asking to sign in again when the token is unknown,
    expired or spent, or a 503 delivery failure.

Receive frontend log entries for centralized logging.

This endpoint allows the frontend to send log entries to the backend
for centralized logging, monitoring, and debugging.

Security:
- Rate limited to 30 reports per minute per client (scope: 'frontend_logs')
- Payload size limited to prevent abuse
- Available to anonymous users but throttled aggressively

Args:
    request: HTTP request object
    payload: Frontend log entry data

Returns:
    Success response with 201 status or error response with appropriate status

Raises:
    HttpError: 400 for validation errors, 413 for payload too large, 500 for server errors

get.description:
Check application and database readiness with a query on the default connection.

Return healthy when SELECT 1 succeeds, or a fixed service-unavailable response
when the database cannot answer. This endpoint does not check Redis.
Returns a list of all API error codes. This endpoint exposes error codes and categories for frontend type generation via OpenAPI.

Health check endpoint for the logging system.

This endpoint verifies that the logging system is working correctly
and can receive frontend logs.

Args:
    request: HTTP request object

Returns:
    Health status response with correlation ID and timestamp

Raises:
    HttpError: 500 if logging system is unhealthy

post.description:
Development-only endpoint to write browser console logs to file.

This endpoint receives formatted log lines from the frontend logger
and appends them to backend/logs/frontend.log for AI debugging.

Args:
    request: HTTP request object
    payload: Request body holding the formatted log line to write to file

Returns:
    Status response indicating success or failure

Security:
    - Only available when ENVIRONMENT is development
    - No authentication required (localhost development only)
    - File path is fixed to prevent directory traversal

get.description:
Development-only endpoint that returns a 500 error for testing.

Use this to verify frontend error handling (e.g., toast notifications
for server errors).

Security:
    - Only available when ENVIRONMENT is development
    - Returns 403 in production

get.description:
Browse movies with advanced filtering options and user-specific data.

Newest-first without an explicit year or date constraint defaults to films
released through today in UTC. Explicit year and date filters retain control
over the browsing range. The service layer applies this default for all callers.

This endpoint implements a two-pass filtering architecture:
1. TMDB API filtering (primary) - Reduces millions of movies to thousands
2. Backend filtering (second-pass) - Catches TMDB data quality issues

The schema layer extracts parameters for both passes from incoming filter
parameters. For example, release_date_gte="2020-01-01" generates both:
- release_date.gte for TMDB API (primary filter)
- year_min=2020 for backend filtering (data hygiene)

This ensures users see only movies matching their filters, even when TMDB
API returns movies with incorrect release dates or ratings.

Uses FilterSchema to handle 40+ optional parameters cleanly, with automatic
empty string to None conversion to handle Django Ninja 1.4.3 + Pydantic 2.12.0
validation behavior.

Query Parameters (all in filters schema):
    filters: MovieDiscoverFilterSchema with all TMDB discover parameters
        - page: Page number for pagination (default: 1)
        - with_genres: Comma-separated genre IDs to include
        - genres: Alias for with_genres (frontend convenience)
        - decade: Decade filter (e.g., "1990s" → converts to date range)
        - sort_by: Sort criteria (popularity.desc, vote_average.desc, etc.)
        - vote_average_gte/lte: Rating range filtering (both TMDB + backend)
        - release_date_gte/lte: Date range filtering (both TMDB + backend)
        - primary_release_year: Filter by release year
        - [... many other TMDB discover parameters]

Returns:
    MovieListResponseSchema: Paginated list of movies with user data if authenticated

Raises:
    HttpError: 400 for invalid parameters, or 502, 503 or 504 when TMDB fails,
        is busy or times out

Retrieve detailed information for a specific movie by TMDB ID.

MovieDiscoverFilterSchema.description:
Schema for TMDB discover endpoint filtering with two-pass architecture.

Extracts parameters for both:
1. TMDB API filtering (primary) - Reduces millions of movies to thousands
2. Backend filtering (second-pass) - Catches TMDB data quality issues

For example, release_date_gte="2020-01-01" generates:
- release_date.gte for TMDB API (primary filter)
- year_min=2020 for backend filtering (data hygiene)

Handles 40+ optional query parameters with automatic empty string to None
conversion, solving Django Ninja 1.4.3 + Pydantic 2.12.0 validation issues
where missing parameters are sent as empty strings instead of being omitted.

See: External research on Django Ninja optional parameter handling (2025-10-09)

MovieListItemSchema.description:
Compact movie representation for list/grid endpoints.

Contains essential display fields optimized for browse, search, and collection views.
Uses genre_ids (integers) rather than full genre objects for efficiency.

Extended by MovieDetailSchema for single-movie detail views, which adds full
genre objects, cast, crew, certifications, and other detailed information.
MovieListItemSchema.title: MovieListItemSchema

MovieListResponseSchema.description:
Response envelope for movie collection endpoints.

Used for all endpoints returning multiple movies: browse, search, discover,
user collections, etc. Supports optional pagination via page/total_pages fields.

The next_tmdb_page_start field enables cursor-based pagination for TMDB-backed
endpoints with the smart buffer mechanism; null signals their exhaustion.
Database-served collections always leave it null and use page < total_pages
to indicate another page.

next_tmdb_page_start.description: Next TMDB page to fetch for pagination continuation (smart buffer tracking)
next_tmdb_page_start.title: Next Tmdb Page Start
